structured_output.hypothesis: If the claim holds, then for adult ox (Bos), sheep (Ovis) and giraffe (Giraffa) metacarpals, shaft breadth scaled to equal bone length is about 2/3 of the ox value in sheep and about 1/3 of the ox value in giraffe, and the length-breadth proportions otherwise match.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using per-specimen greatest length (GL) and a breadth measure (smallest shaft breadth or mid-shaft breadth), compute the relative slenderness B/GL per taxon. Pass if the taxon-mean ratio of (sheep B/GL)/(ox B/GL) lies in 0.57-0.77 and (giraffe B/GL)/(ox B/GL) lies in 0.27-0.40. Also pass only if the ratios hold across both proximal and distal breadth, within 15% of each other (a simple one-axis stretch).
structured_output.fail_criterion: Fail if either ratio falls outside those ranges (sheep outside 0.57-0.77 or giraffe outside 0.27-0.40). Fail if proximal-breadth and distal-breadth ratios differ by more than 15%, since that means the bones differ by more than a single-axis stretch.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's "cannon-bone" is the fused metacarpal III+IV (metatarsal in the hindlimb) of the ruminant. His "length" is the long axis of the bone, and his "breadth" is the transverse width. Modern measurements are greatest length (GL) and breadth of the proximal end, shaft (smallest breadth) and distal end, following von den Driesch (1976). "At equal length" is operationalised as the breadth-to-length ratio B/GL, which is size-standardised. This is a modern reinterpretation: Thompson worked from a few figured specimens, while the test uses species means across many specimens.
structured_output.no_dataset_reason: I did not find a public dataset that holds metacarpal length and breadth for ox, sheep and giraffe together and that I could fetch and check. The candidates I searched for and read about were these. The Mendeley Data set "In search of draught cattle" covers cattle only. Ríos, Danowitz and Solounias (2016, Palaeontologia Electronica, doi 10.26879/653) cover giraffids only and I found no data file on the article page. Sheep metapodial measurements exist only as a thesis supplement for sheep. Specimen-level portals such as VertNet and iDigBio, and MorphoSource, may hold the needed measurements, but I did not locate and fetch a specific dataset record for all three taxa. Rather than name an unverified identifier, I set the dataset to null.
